stem: After which incident, Mahatma Gandhi had called Non-cooperation Movement as his "Himalayan Blunder"?
expl: Chauri-Chaura is a town in Gorakhpur district of Uttar Pradesh. Here, on 4 February 1922, a crowd of protesters set fire to a police outpost of the British administration. According to the Chauri-Chaura Martyrs’ Memorial, a total of 23 policemen were killed in this incident. Gandhiji condemned this incident and described it as a “Himalayan blunder.” On 12 February 1922, in the meeting of the Congress Working Committee held at Bardoli, it was decided to suspend the movement. Regarding his decision to end the movement, Gandhiji wrote in ‘Young India’ that— “To save the movement from turning violent, I am ready to bear every insult, every suffering, complete boycott, and even death.”

Indicate the true sequence of events concerning the postponement of Non-cooperation Movement :
(1) Police firing in Chauri-Chaura
(2) Police station set fired by violent crowd
(3) Postponement of Movement by Gandhiji
(4) Arresting of Gandhiji
Select your answer from the following codes –
expl: On 4 February 1922, a Congress and Khilafat procession was taken out at Chauri-Chaura (Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh). Some policemen misbehaved with them; as a result, a group within the procession attacked the police. The police opened fire, which further enraged the crowd, and the crowd again attacked the police. The policemen ran into the police station, and the crowd set it on fire. After receiving news of this incident, Gandhiji decided to withdraw the movement. In the Congress Working Committee meeting held at Bardoli on 12 February 1922, it was decided to suspend the movement. Taking advantage of this situation, the government arrested him on 10 March 1922 and, on 18 March 1922, sentenced him to six years’ imprisonment. Thus, option (a) is the correct answer.

stem:
Regarding the Non-Cooperation Movement in towns, which of the following statements are NOT correct?
(1) Only the upper castes and the rich participated in the movement.
(2) The Justice Party of Madras also boycotted the council elections.
(3) Thousands of students left government-controlled schools; headmasters and teachers resigned; and lawyers gave up their practice.

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The Non-Cooperation Movement was formally launched on 1 August 1920. In it, thousands of students left government-controlled schools, headmasters and teachers submitted resignation letters, and lawyers gave up their legal practice. It is noteworthy that people from both urban and rural areas participated in this movement, and it was the largest mass movement of the freedom struggle up to that time. In the council elections held then, the Justice Party of Madras participated and won 63 seats.

stem: What was the purpose for which C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party within the Congress?

options.label: a
options.text: To lead the struggle of the general public

options.label: c
options.text: To participate in elections to the State Councils

options.label: d
options.text: For legislative opposition against the Rowlatt Act

expl: On 31 December 1922, in a meeting held at the residence of the Maharaja of Tikari in Gaya, the formation of a new party within the Congress—‘Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party’ was announced. In 1923, the ‘Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party’ (Swaraj Party) was formed, and from 20–22 February 1923, the general meeting of this newly formed party was held in Allahabad (present-day Prayagraj). In this meeting, the party’s programme and constitution were approved and the party was given the new name ‘Swaraj Party’. C.R. Das became its President and Motilal Nehru became its General Secretary. This party was formed with the objective of contesting council elections while remaining within the Congress. It also participated in the elections to the State Councils as well as the Central Legislative Council and achieved good success. Their real aim was to enter these assemblies, present their views, and practise non-cooperation with the government from within. The Swaraj Party was established after the failure of the Non-Cooperation Movement.
